prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by chemically induced proximity, from bifunctional PROTACs that recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glue degraders.

statement.case_for: I keep B057 as my single-part preference. Induced proximity is a new chemical mode of action: a designed bridge or a glue reshapes a protein surface so that the cell's ubiquitin-proteasome machinery removes the target catalytically, instead of a ligand occupying a site. The mechanism (ternary-complex formation, E3 substrate selectivity, cereblon as the thalidomide target) has been independently confirmed across many laboratories, E3 ligases and target classes, so the open question is clinical and not scientific. Crews and Deshaies supplied the concept and first cellular demonstrations; Handa's cereblon work supplied the mechanism that unifies PROTACs and glues and explains a decades-old pharmacological puzzle. Round 1 showed five explicit supporters with an identical trio and all eight members naming B057 as preferred or first alternative, and that breadth comes from members with very different fields, which I treat as corroboration and not as a substitute for the scientific argument.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so the committee could fairly judge the field a few years early, and I cannot dismiss that. The three-name cap leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim, each with a real claim, and the PROTAC and glue strands have distinct histories, so one citation risks reading as two achievements joined together. I also accept that B054 and B068 are more mature and more cleanly attributed, though maturity is not the same as superiority.

responses.point: Brzezinski argues that choosing Handa over Ciulli is a decision about the scope of the discovery, that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made rational PROTAC design possible, and that the committee should wait until credit between the two arms settles.
responses.response: I agree it is a scope decision and I have tried to make it explicitly. My changed view is that I now state the citation so that it names cereblon and the glue mechanism as the second pillar beside the PROTAC concept, because that is what Handa is credited for, and I accept that this leaves Ciulli's structural work in the field but outside the credited names. I still place Handa above Ciulli because cereblon underlies the largest clinical class and the thalidomide mechanism, whereas VHL ligands refined a design concept that Crews and Deshaies had already shown works. On waiting, I think the credit is unlikely to become clearer with time; the lineages are already well documented, and the unresolved item is clinical approval, which is a different kind of uncertainty from a priority dispute.

responses.point: Somfai holds that the PROTAC concept and the cereblon discovery are two different discoveries, one design-driven and one mechanistic, that eight names cannot be fairly compressed into three, and that the field could settle first.
responses.response: I accept that they are two lineages, but I read them as converging on one conceptual achievement, since cereblon shows that thalidomide-class glues work by the same ternary-complex, E3-recruitment logic as a designed bifunctional molecule. That is why the citation says chemically induced proximity and not two separate inventions. The cap is uncomfortable, but a cap that excludes deserving people is a feature of every prize and not specific to this one. I take his point seriously enough that if the committee cannot agree that the strands form one achievement, I would move to a fallback instead of forcing a split trio, and my fallback is B054 over B068 for the reason I give below.

responses.point: Zou prefers B068, stating that C-N coupling is a general, original and fully mature method with clean two-person attribution, that the 2010 prize covered C-C coupling only, and she would support B057 if the clinical evidence is judged sufficient.
responses.response: The chair asked whether the distinction from 2010 can be stated, and Zou's answer, that C-N bond formation needed its own ligand design and mechanistic understanding of amine binding and reductive elimination, is a fair one that moves me somewhat. I had treated B068 mainly as an extension of the 2010 class and I now regard that as too dismissive; it is a distinct bond construction with its own mechanism. It does not change my preference, because I still weigh a new mode of action above a mature method, but it makes B068 my second alternative. On her clinical condition, I would say the evidence of late-stage degrader trials plus extensive mechanistic confirmation is sufficient for a prize that honours the chemical concept.

responses.point: Linke's round-1 case notes that the PROTAC and glue strands have different histories and that a single citation may blur two achievements, and he names B054 as the safer choice if that blur is unacceptable; his summary also asks whether the lack of an approved drug makes the prize premature.
responses.response: On the chair's timing question, my answer is that I would award now: previous prizes have recognised enabling chemical concepts before the full clinical story closed, and here the mechanism is not in doubt. I agree that B054 is the right fallback if the blur is judged unacceptable, because it has a coherent three-person split and no clinical question. I would not want the fallback to be treated as equal to B057 on conceptual novelty, but I would vote for it over a contested trio.

responses.point: Sparr moved from B005 to B057, keeps B005 as a first alternative, and raises whether PROTACs and molecular glues might be better recognised as two separate prize parts.
responses.response: I raised the two-part split myself earlier and I now oppose it. With a three-name cap, two parts would give each strand one or two names and weaken both, and the unifying point is the induced-proximity mechanism. Sparr's note that B057 is better resolved than B005 on maturity and credit matches my reading, and her disclosure about overlap with B005 and B064 is another reason I have dropped B005 as my alternative in favour of B054 and B068.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the absence of an approved degrader as compatible with a prize now.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name; I have settled on Handa but I hold this with moderate confidence.
Whether PROTACs and glues will be read as one achievement under induced proximity or as two joined together.
My recollection of priority and clinical status is not independently verified from the supplied materials.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to any credited candidate on the shortlist. I note a field closeness to peptide, protein and biosensing chemistry and a research overlap with Emma Sparr on self-assembly, which bears on B005 and B064 and not on B057, and no recusal is needed. This disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
